findings.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:76 — Role/client/group removal listener gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ instead of V2 flag, so permissions-enabled reset is silently skipped for V2-only deployments

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:499 — hasPermission fallback lacks admin-role short-circuit used elsewhere, denying role-mapping to admins who should be allowed via canManage

services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:391 — canManageClientScopes duplicates canManage logic instead of delegating, risking future divergence

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:499 — hasPermission fallback lacks admin-role short-circuit used elsewhere, denying role-mapping to admins who should be allowed via canManage

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2`, the role-mapping checks (`canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, `canMapClientScopeRoles`) return only `hasPermission(client, <scope>)` and do not short-circuit on admin roles (e.g., `AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS`) or on `canManage(client)` the way `canManage(ClientModel)`/`canManage()`/`canView()` do. If the intended semantics are that admin roles (or manage) should implicitly allow these operations, this implementation could unexpectedly deny them. However, that intent is not provable from this diff alone (and the finding’s cited line number doesn’t match the new file length), so it’s best treated as a specific design/consistency concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:391 — canManageClientScopes duplicates canManage logic instead of delegating, risking future divergence

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canManageClientScopes()` repeats the same basic authorization pattern used elsewhere (checking `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` and then `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`) instead of delegating to an existing method like `canManage()` which already combines an admin-role check (`super.canManage()`) with the same `MANAGE` permission. This is a maintainability/consistency concern (risk of divergence if `super.canManage()` logic changes), not a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone. The cited line number is inaccurate (file is ~287 lines), but the duplication claim is grounded in the shown method bodies.
